judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/recital language for an endorsement; the only oddity is the scanning typo 'te exercise' and a stray period, neither of which changes meaning. Nothing here names an operative term a court would have to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply introduces the Discovery Period Activation amendments and is consistent with Section III (c037) and the Declarations Item 4 (c012). No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference is garbled ('Section XDI' for Section XIII), and it fixes a single termination date and hour, which is otherwise definite. The mechanical error is an artifact rather than a meaning-changing defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the amended Policy Period in c020 (to 05/13/2009) but sits against Section XIII (c104-c106), which describes cancellation/conversion rather than expiry, and against the Discovery Period trigger in c037 which requires cancellation or nonrenewal rather than mere expiration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short pointer sentence introducing the coverage table; 'Section II]' is an OCR garble of Section III but the referent is obvious. Nothing ambiguous in its own right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Discovery Period Activation subject to Section III (c037), which is consistent; the listed coverages track Item 6 (c014). No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on whether the acquiring entity is 'legally permitted to indemnify' regardless of actual indemnification — a phrase that has generated real disputes about presumptive indemnification. 'Such Loss' has no clear antecedent in the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels but does not exactly track Section VII(B)(2) (c091) and Section VIII(A)(2) (c093), which speak of the Company rather than an acquiring entity, and it presupposes an acquisition even though this endorsement deletes Section XII (c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement definition of 'Company' brings in 'the acquiring entity' — an undefined term — and limits coverage to Wrongful Acts 'involving' the Item 1 entities, a notably elastic word. The double limitation ('only for ... and only for') invites argument about its reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the Section IV definition of Company (c042), which itself refers to Section XII(B) — a section this same endorsement deletes (c006) — so the defined term now sits awkwardly with c102/c180.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat deletion of a named section; nothing in the sentence itself is ambiguous or mis-drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleting Section XII entirely leaves the definition of Company (c042), the Subsidiary Wrongful Acts Exclusion (c077) and the Fiduciary 'Insured' definition (c152) cross-referring to a section that no longer exists, and it sits against the Mergers Endorsement's statement that all other provisions of Section XII remain unchanged (c181).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite, single-purpose statement that the Discovery Period premium is fully earned and noncancellable. No term requires construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same rule in Section III (c037), and is consistent with the return-premium provisions in c104/c105. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date and hour; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement takes effect at the same moment the Policy terminates under c002 and c020, which is coherent for an extended reporting period but does put the two dates in immediate juxtaposition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate; 'other than as above stated' is a familiar formula with an accepted meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the substantive changes in the same endorsement (c005, c006) it is self-limiting rather than contradictory, and it mirrors c023, c028 and c183.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain notice that this is a claims-made, no-duty-to-defend policy with defense costs inside the limit; no term is left uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the same rule as Section IX(A)(1) (c095) and Section VII(A) (c090), so it reinforces rather than contradicts the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dollar cap stated per Policy Year; the only defect is the OCR garble 'paovises' for 'provided', which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The individual Insuring Agreement limits in Item 8 sum to far more than the $10,000,000 total, so this Item must be harmonised with Section VII(A)(1)-(2) (c090) and the non-erosion provision (c093), a fit that is workable but not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States a 75% premium and 365-day length definitely; 'if the eligibility requirements are met' is an unspecified cross-reference but plainly points to Section III.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section III (c037) computes the premium by reference to 'the percentage set forth in Item 4', and the actual Discovery Period Activation charged different amounts per coverage, which creates a possible mismatch with this Item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare notice address; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section X(C) (c099) points here for notices, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A condition on coverage stated in definite terms — limit, retention and premium must all appear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats Section I's opening condition (c031); several endorsement Insuring Agreements (c128, c145, c165) rely on Item 6 entries, and the table shows those entries, so no conflict emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence enumerates specific coverages folded into Insuring Agreement (C) and then conditions their exclusion on a 'different Limit of Liability or retention' being 'desired' — a subjective trigger whose operation is far from clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 6 shows separate limits for Securities Liability, and the Securities Liability Exclusion endorsement (c124) and Securities Liability Insuring Agreement (c165) do exactly what this sentence contemplates, so its interaction with Insuring Agreement (C) scope is a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets a $5,000 retention with a garbled cross-reference ('Section ITV (X)(2)') and then a second sentence that redirects to Item 9 if coverage comes by endorsement, which is potentially self-cancelling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section IV(X)(2) (c061) and the reinstatement provision in Section VII(A)(4) (c090), and no IRA/Keogh limit is shown in Item 6, leaving the provision partly inoperative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The endorsement list is materially garbled at its end ('500! | 5 0€ > aH'), so the set of documents incorporated cannot be read off the face of the Item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The three successive Declarations amendments (c021, c026) list different endorsement sets, so which endorsements form part of the Policy at any given date is not resolvable from one Item alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration-style statement identifying the constituent documents; definite in expression.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the 'Policy' definition (c054) and the entire-agreement clause (c113), which lists a slightly different set of documents (Policy, Application, Endorsements, not Declarations expressly), a small but real mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bare recital introducing a Declarations amendment; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other amendment preambles (c024, c123). No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two dated periods stated precisely; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-month extension interacts with the 'Policy Year' definition (c056), which provides that any extension forms part of the Policy Year that would have ended on the original expiration date, and with the Discovery Period deeming rule in c037.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of form numbers; nothing intrinsically ambiguous, though it silently adds and drops forms relative to earlier lists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from Item 13 as originally issued (c017) and as amended in c026, so the operative endorsement set depends on which version of Item 13 governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Effective 04/13/2009, the original expiry date, which is coherent with the extension it effects in c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Self-limiting against the changes made in the same endorsement; mirrors c009 and c028.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bare recital; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other amendment preambles. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of named entities with a scanning typo ('Fisst Federal'); the substitution itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'Named Insured' means the first entity listed in Item 1 (c053), placing Vantus Bank first silently changes who receives notice, cancels and acts for all Insureds under c105, c115 and c104.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of form numbers; nothing intrinsically uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in content with the Item 13 lists in c017 and c021, so the governing endorsement schedule is version-dependent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of the endorsement. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Self-limiting; mirrors c009 and c023.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain notice of claims-made and no-duty-to-defend structure; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeats c010 and tracks c090 and c095; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consideration clause subjecting coverage to the Policy's terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c031 and c038's incorporation of the Application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite condition precedent to any Insuring Agreement operating; no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Item 6 (c014) and governs the endorsement Insuring Agreements (c128, c145, c165), all of which have Item 6 entries, so no inconsistency appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except for Loss the Company pays as indemnification' is a short phrase that decides whether A-side coverage is displaced, and 'pays' sits uneasily against the presumptive-indemnification concept used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII(B)(2) (c091) and Section VIII(A)(2) (c093) apply the (B) retention whether or not indemnification is actually granted, which pulls in a different direction from a carve-out keyed to what the Company actually pays.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'has agreed to or is legally permitted or required by law to indemnify' is the standard but genuinely contested trigger for B-side coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the retention rules in c091 and the order-of-payments provision in c094; the fit is workable but the permitted/required distinction recurs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short grant of entity coverage for Wrongful Acts; the heading is garbled ('es') but the operative words are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is cut down by the Securities Liability Exclusion (c124), the Item 6 note in c015 and the Section VI exclusions (c079-c089), so its practical reach depends on other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is garbled ('a)' paired with '(2)'), and the final sentence's exclusion of loss 'arising from any act or omission by' the estate or spouse could swallow much of the grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Insured Person definition (c048) and the Wrongful Act definition (c061); no direct conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at the direction of the Company' and the excess-of-other-indemnification proviso are the kind of short qualifiers that can be read two ways, but the provision is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted for three of the five purchased coverages (c130, c147, c167), so its survival is patchy across the instrument, and it overlaps the excess clause in c118.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is limited to cancellation, nonrenewal or conversion 'subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)', and the bar on notice of circumstances during the Discovery Period is a hard rule with significant consequences; several phrases here are worth fighting over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XIII(C)(2) (c106) says the occurrence of ANY of the conversion events — including Financial Impairment under (C)(1)(a) — shall not affect the right to purchase the Discovery Period, which cannot be squared with this section's limitation to (C)(1)(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all applications, attachments and materials submitted to the Insurer' for this or any predecessor policy is a sweeping and boundary-less description of the incorporated documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the entire-agreement clause (c113) and the representations/severability provisions (c109-c111), which turn on what the Application contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A defined-term list closing with broad additions ('economic advice, financial advice', 'financial planning advice including without limitation') and then carve-outs, which is exactly the general-versus-specific structure that produces scope fights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives both the Section V(B) exclusion (c064) and the Brokerage Insuring Agreement (c128), so the same words both grant and exclude coverage depending on the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a written or oral demand for monetary damages or non-monetary relief' is a notoriously contested formulation, and the trailing qualifier 'for a Wrongful Act including any appeal from such proceeding' attaches unclearly to the whole list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition governs the notice provisions (c097, c098), the single-claim rule (c092) and the Discovery Period reporting rule (c037), so its boundaries have knock-on effects throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line statutory definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in c160; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure, though it fixes Subsidiary status by reference to the inception date and then admits later bank Subsidiaries only 'subject to Section XII (B)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is replaced for the Discovery Period by c005 and depends on Section XII(B), which the Mergers Endorsement rewrites (c180) and the Discovery Period endorsement deletes altogether (c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses' is a standard but genuinely elastic phrase, and the exclusion of 'overhead' has fuzzy edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the advancement and allocation provisions (c096, c107, c108) which give the Insurer power to test reasonableness; the fit is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statute is misnamed ('Employment Retirement Income Security Act'), but the reference is unmistakable and the error does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in c067 and c145/c153; consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition excepts 'Leased Employee or Independent Contractor' in capitalised form, yet neither is defined anywhere, leaving the carve-out's boundary unfixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IV contains no definition of either capitalised term, so the exception cannot be resolved from the rest of the instrument, and Employee feeds the Insured Person definition (c048) and the Fiduciary endorsement definitions (c149-c151).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is closed and specific — appointment of a receiver or similar official, or debtor in possession — with little room for argument on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge between the Insolvency Exclusion (c083), which excludes claims 'involving' Financial Impairment, and Section XVI(I) (c120), which says Financial Impairment shall not release the Insurer; those two pull in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-element definition; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fiduciary endorsement replaces this definition (c152), so 'Insured' has two meanings depending on which coverage is engaged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'officer' and 'honorary or advisory director' are undefined and the class covers past, present and future persons, but the formulation is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'Company' includes Subsidiaries (c042), the class of Insured Persons expands and contracts with c005 and c077; that interaction is workable but not trivial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed five-item list of services with no catch-all; comparatively tight drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Section V(I) exclusion (c071) and its credit-life carve-out; consistent with c039's parallel carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'common nexus any fact, circumstance, situation, event, transaction or series of related facts' is a relatedness formula that courts repeatedly find susceptible to competing readings of how loose the nexus may be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls the single-claim rule (c092), the Prior Notice Exclusion (c074), the Subsidiary exclusion (c077) and c103, so a broad or narrow reading materially changes several other provisions.
